v.rationale: All three passed their own suites (impl-2: 13 tests; impl-1 and impl-3: 11 each). They share the same core: a #[Scope] inactiveFor with a grouped whereNull/orWhere, a nullable timestamp column, an attribute-based command, and Schedule::command()->dailyAt('06:00')->appendOutputTo(). In my probes all three behaved the same. Each accepts '0', ' 3' and '+3', and each rejects empty, null, and an overflowing --days value. All gave the correct count for very large N. Each wrote its scheduled output to the log file. So the ranking comes down to tests, proportionality and polish. impl-2 has the strongest tests: freezeTime, a boundary check on both sides with subSecond, a factory state, and a dataset of invalid inputs that includes empty. It also has the leanest validation (filter_var with min_range) and an indexed column. It loses a little for Http::preventStrayRequests noise, an incidental onOneServer assertion, bare-number log output and a duplicated comment line in Pest.php. impl-1 is close. It has labelled log output, a boundary test and a clean Pest.php edit. But it adds withoutOverlapping(10), which is unneeded ceremony and a cache-lock dependency for a trivial count on a single server, and its tests are slightly less thorough. impl-3 comes last. It prints '1 users', its imports fail Pint, it uses a heavyweight Validator for one option, it has no index, and it doesn't freeze time or test the boundary. Its invalid-input assertion is also loose.
